cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You called my audition interesting. What came after that in your head?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then give me the encouraging half and the half you swallowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better by how much? Are we buying dance lessons or shoes that don't move?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks the hidden thought and A3 commands both halves, but A5 ordinary what-to-buy question does not consistently carry superior approval beyond stock phrases.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to encourage a sister and B4 offers a cautious comparison, giving the inquiry a real reason to continue.

heightening.evidence: B4 better singing still hides how bad dancing is, causing A5 practical alternatives testing severity.

specificity.evidence: A1 audition and B4 singing/dancing establish feedback context without needing a performance transcript.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 immobile shoes is a specific exaggeration from B4 dance criticism, but stock rank wording is clumsy.
